title: Netflix Bets on Kargil War Drama as Its Biggest Indian Series Yet
excerpt: Operation Safed Saagar, based on the IAF's 17th Squadron during the 1999 Kargil conflict, brings Top Gun-scale aerial combat to Indian streaming with cooperation from the Indian Air Force.
body:
• Netflix's Operation Safed Saagar recreates the Indian Air Force's high-altitude bombing campaign during the 1999 Kargil War, marking the streamer's most ambitious Indian production.
  • The series was the only Indian title featured at Netflix's global What Next? 2026 event, signaling a push for worldwide appeal beyond diaspora audiences.
  • Filmed on actual IAF bases with military cooperation, the show stars Siddharth and Jimmy Shergill and is created by the teams behind Panchayat and Asur.
  • The production follows a wave of Indian air warfare films inspired by Top Gun: Maverick, including Fighter (2024) and Sky Force (2025).

Netflix has unveiled its most ambitious Indian original yet: Operation Safed Saagar, a Hindi-language drama series set during the 1999 Kargil War between India and Pakistan. The show, announced at a military event on November 1, 2025, was described by the streamer as "what promises to be Netflix's biggest Indian series of 2026."

The Real Operation Behind the Series

The series dramatizes the story of the Golden Arrows, the Indian Air Force's 17th Squadron, during Operation Safed Sagar — Hindi for "White Ocean." The real-life military campaign saw IAF pilots conduct bombing runs at altitudes where no air force in the world had previously operated, a feat that fundamentally changed India's approach to high-altitude aerial warfare.

At the center of the narrative is Squadron Commander B.S. Dhanoa, whose wingman, Squadron Leader Ajay Ahuja, was killed by enemy forces. According to Netflix's official synopsis, Dhanoa's squadron "turns the tide of the war by leading attacks on Pakistani troops, bombing at heights at which no Air Force in the world has ever operated."

"This is also the story of how these fighter pilots are physically, mentally and socially transformed to go that extra mile and achieve the impossible."

— Netflix official synopsis

A-List Creative Team

The series is created by Abhijeet Singh Parmar, known for the critically acclaimed Panchayat, alongside Kushal Srivastava. Direction comes from Oni Sen, who helmed the thriller series Asur. Writing duties fall to Sandeep Jain (Kota Factory), Nikhil Ravi (IC 814: The Kandahar Hijack), and Barun Kashyap.

The ensemble cast features Siddharth, Jimmy Shergill (Choona), Abhay Verma (Munjya), Taaruk Raina (Mismatched), Mihir Ahuja (The Archies), and Arnav Bhasin (Cubicles). Production is handled by Matchbox Shots LLP, the company behind Scoop, alongside Feel Good Films.

Netflix's Global Ambitions for Indian Content

The show's significance extends beyond its subject matter. Operation Safed Saagar was the sole Indian title featured at Netflix's global Next on Netflix 2026 event, branded What Next? — a distinction that suggests the company views it as a crossover title capable of drawing international audiences, not just Indian viewers.

Netflix secured cooperation from the Indian Air Force for the production, gaining access to film on actual IAF bases. This military partnership ensured technical accuracy in depicting aerial operations, equipment, and protocol — a detail that distinguishes the series from recent Bollywood air warfare films that relied more heavily on creative license.

Riding the Air Combat Wave

The series arrives amid renewed interest in Indian air warfare stories, a trend partly fueled by the global success of Top Gun: Maverick in 2022. Bollywood responded with Fighter starring Hrithik Roshan in 2024 and Sky Force in 2025, both set against India-Pakistan aerial conflicts.

But where those films compressed their narratives into two-hour runtimes, Operation Safed Saagar has the breathing room of a multi-episode series to explore not just combat sequences but the psychological toll on pilots operating at the edge of what was thought physically possible.

What It Means for Indian Streaming

For Netflix, the investment reflects a broader strategic shift. Indian content appeared in the platform's Global Top 10 every week through 2024 and 2025, with viewing hours crossing 3.4 billion in 2025 across 75 countries. Over 70 percent of global viewing of Indian titles happened via subtitles or dubbing, reaching audiences in Latin America, North Africa, and East Asia.

The streamer recently opened Eyeline Studios, its global VFX and production facility, in Hyderabad — its fifth global location after Los Angeles, Vancouver, Seoul, and London. A release date for Operation Safed Saagar has not been announced, but Netflix has positioned it as a flagship title for 2026.
